title: Inventing Anna
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: A con unravelling is a propulsive true-crime shape and Garner's performance carries it, but its own prediction flags the nine-episode runtime as stretched — the padding is what keeps it off 5.

title: Maestro in Blue
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Atmospheric Greek island romance with light crime threads — slow, mood-led and subtitled, which blocks half-attention viewing. Pleasant to sit with rather than compelling forward.

title: Marvel's Luke Cage
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: The Netflix-Marvel thirteen-episode format is notorious for mid-season sag, and its own prediction says S2 drags. Completionist pull rather than momentum; Jessica Jones is the stronger entry in this universe.

title: Marvel's The Defenders
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Only eight episodes with a crossover team-up structure that moves fast — the shortest and most plot-driven entry in the Netflix-Marvel run. Weak Hand storyline caps the pull, but the low commitment makes it easy to clear.

title: Modern Love Tokyo
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Standalone anthology romance — every episode resets, so there is no forward pull by design. Very low commitment and easy to dip into, which is its appeal, but structurally the opposite of a binge engine.

title: Patriot
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Deadpan melancholic pacing with long digressive tangents — the tone is the pleasure and it is deliberately unhurried. Cult-adored but effortful, and cancelled without resolution removes the payoff incentive to push on.

title: Psych
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Eight seasons of pure case-of-the-week with a full reset each episode. Monk is the stated comp and you abandoned it after eight episodes — 'the show doesn't seem to go anywhere'. Breezy and light, but no hook and a huge cold-start back catalogue.

title: Rectify
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 2/5: Famously the slowest prestige drama of its era — long silences, interior stillness, almost no plot velocity, across four seasons. Its own prediction stacks slow-burn and dark-without-hope penalties. Genuinely hard to keep going.

title: Roseanne
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Classic multi-cam family sitcom — self-contained episodes, no serialisation, and ten seasons of cold-start back catalogue. Easy comfort viewing in bursts, but nothing pulls forward and late seasons are uneven.

title: Secret Level
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Anthology of unconnected animated shorts, so momentum resets every episode, and its own prediction calls it wildly uneven — more showcase reel than story. Easy to sample, nothing to continue.

title: See
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Quest-and-pursuit structure across short seasons with regular action beats, so it does move. Action-over-character focus means low investment, which caps the pull at 4.

title: Shoresy
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Very short episodes and a season-long hockey campaign arc make it structurally easy to keep going. Niche dialect humour is the risk to engagement rather than momentum — hence 4 on this axis despite the 3★ rating call.

title: Smoke
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Arson investigation with a serialised hunt across a short complete run — a case engine with a genuine spine. Soft audience reception (49%) suggests the execution may not fully deliver on that structure.

title: SS-GB
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Five-episode murder mystery in occupied Britain, so low commitment, but critics found it slow and murky, and the moody alt-history register drags. Steady rather than gripping.

title: Steal
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Six-episode heist thriller — short, plot-forward and structurally built to pull. Reviews flagging thin writing and weak characters are the reason it stops at 4: momentum without investment tends to stall.

title: Territory
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Yellowstone-style succession fight over a cattle station, with family-saga cliffhangers across six episodes. Soft audience score (54%) and a cancelled single season keep it at 4.

title: The Alienist
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Period serial-killer investigation with a real case spine, but the pacing is stately and the 1890s atmosphere is prioritised over velocity. Grim subject matter makes consecutive episodes heavy.

title: The Blacklist
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Blacklister-of-the-week with a mythology thread — the thread gives some pull, but ten seasons of episodic back catalogue on a cold start is the Monk shape exactly, plus the known S2+ fatigue pattern.

title: The Gray House
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Civil War spy-ring premise has a covert-mission engine, but the early signal is genuinely weak (Trakt 6.5 on a tiny sample, soft TMDB), suggesting execution that does not carry momentum. Unproven.

title: The Middle
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Nine seasons of self-contained family sitcom episodes with no serialisation — pleasant and frictionless in ones, but zero pull, and the back-catalogue bulk is the quiet-abandonment shape.

title: The Perfect Couple
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Six-episode wedding whodunit with soap-opera twists and a fixed suspect list — the closed-question structure that reliably scores 5 for you. Reviews say implausible and glossy, which is a quality problem, not a momentum one.

title: The Sinner
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Each season is a self-contained why-did-they-do-it with a withheld motive, which is a strong hook, and the anthology reset avoids decline. Dark psychological register and drawn-out reveals keep it at 4.

title: Twin Peaks
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 2/5: Deliberately dreamlike and digressive, with a notorious mid-S2 collapse and a Return season that is actively anti-narrative. Its own prediction stacks experimental and slow penalties — a show to study, not to be pulled through.

title: Waiting for the Out
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 2/5: Weekly philosophical discussions with prison inmates — a conversation format with no plot engine at all. Cerebral and static by design; Black Bird (3★, 'didn't mind it') is the nearest comp and had far more narrative drive.

title: Wellington Paranormal
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Case-of-the-week deadpan mockumentary in very short episodes — frictionless to start, but its own prediction calls it thin and repetitive across a full run. Funny in bursts, no forward pull.

title: What's Next? The Future with Bill Gates
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Five standalone talking-heads documentary episodes — low commitment and easy, but each is self-contained with no narrative thread. Informative rather than compelling.

title: Yellowstone
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Ranch-dynasty melodrama with cliffhanger episode endings and strong audience heat (Trakt 8.4) — soap momentum is the top-scoring shape in your data. The messy Costner-departure back half is a quality risk, not a pull problem.

title: You
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 5/5: Stalker-POV thriller with voiceover propulsion and a will-he-be-caught cliffhanger every episode — engineered as a binge object. The rating stays 3★ because the content is a Helen dealbreaker and a dark-character-study risk, but momentum is not the issue.

title: All's Fair
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Ryan Murphy glossy legal soap — a case-and-scandal-per-episode format that is deliberately easy to keep playing. Brutal quality signals (Trakt 5.6, TMDB 4.8) mean the pull may not survive the writing, so 4 not 5.

title: Amazing Stories
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Standalone anthology episodes with no connecting thread, and reviews call the entries forgettable (41% critics). Easy to sample, nothing to continue — anthologies without a frame reset momentum every time.

title: Constellation
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: A reality-is-wrong mystery hook should drive hard, but execution is slow and ambiguous by design, and it was cancelled with the central mystery unresolved — so there is no payoff to pull toward. Weak hook, no payoff.

title: Dr. Brain
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Memory-sync investigation gives it a case spine across six episodes, but subtitled Korean plus moody deliberate pacing adds friction, and the cancelled unresolved ending removes the payoff incentive.

title: Euphoria
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: Visually hypnotic with real melodramatic pull, but structurally episodic character portraits and relentlessly bleak addiction content make consecutive viewing heavy. Style-forward rather than plot-driven.

title: Future Man
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Short half-hour episodes with a time-travel mission arc and constant gags — structurally quick and easy. Raunchy-bro register is real friction for you, which is why the star prediction sits at 2.5★ while momentum stays decent.

title: KAOS
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Eight episodes of interweaving Greek-myth plots with a prophecy engine pulling forward, and Goldblum is watchable throughout. Cancelled on a cliffhanger, so the payoff never arrives — that is the rating problem, not the pull.

title: The Last Frontier
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Manhunt-in-the-wilderness premise with escaped-convict jeopardy is inherently propulsive across a short season. Critics panned it (29%), so the execution likely undercuts the structure — hence 4, not higher.

title: The Lying Life of Adults
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 2/5: Slow subtitled literary coming-of-age with minimal plot — its own prediction identifies it as the exact 'nothing happens' profile that sank The Artful Dodger at 2.5★. Subtitles plus stillness is the lowest-momentum combination here.

title: The Peripheral
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 4/5: Gibson mystery-box with VR-future reveals and episode-end hooks — genuinely propulsive sci-fi. Cancelled on a cliffhanger means the payoff never lands, which is what caps the rating rather than the momentum.

title: The Witcher
predictedBingeabilityReason: Binge 3/5: S1's scrambled non-linear timelines are actively confusing, which its own prediction flags, and the early structure is monster-of-the-week. Recasting mid-run breaks investment further. Some action pull, weak coherence.
